blindSummary: The capital's own council has twice voted to delete anti-discrimination protection, and Pride is contested by the city. (1) 26 April 2024: the capital's metropolitan council passed a bill abolishing the student human-rights ordinance — 12 years after its promulgation — which had prohibited teachers from discriminating on grounds including gender, sexual orientation and gender identity; the council is controlled by the conservative governing party; abolition triggered protests, the identical bill has now passed a second time and the matter is before the supreme court; UN special procedures transmitted a communication on the repeal, with education offices filing observations as enforcing authorities. (2) Pride as contested civic space: the city's mayor uses municipal power against LGBTQ+ gatherings, and the city hosted a mass anti-LGBTQ+ rally claiming 1.1 million participants (organisers; police estimates lower) — described as the largest religious gathering in the country's history. Counterweight: the opposition parliamentary majority announced national student-rights legislation overriding regional offices' decisions, so the repeal is contested and may be overturned by parliament. Judicial rulings from this record's sources: (a) the capital's central district court held that police advice telling a trans person mid-registration-change to "avoid public restrooms for a while" infringed personal rights, awarding 300,000 units of local currency out of a 3 million-unit claim, final 2 July 2024, calling comfortable restroom use "a fundamental and universal human right"; a national human rights commission survey (2021, 591 trans respondents) found 41% had used a restroom of a different gender than their identity out of fear of unfair treatment, 39% avoided food and drink to avoid restrooms and 36% went without; a 2021 regional district court awarded 7 million units of local currency in damages against a beauty academy that barred a trans student's restroom use; (b) a regional court approved gender change for five transgender people without reassignment surgery (8 May 2024), holding that mandatory surgery violates bodily integrity and downgrading prior surgical guidelines to reference status. The state/province hosts the country's largest queer scene, and courts protect the annual queer festival.
blindSourceSummaries: National English-language daily (22 Jul 2024): the capital's central district court ruled that a police officer's advice to a transgender person undergoing legal gender change — "avoid using public restrooms for a while" — infringed personal rights, awarding 300,000 units of local currency out of a 3 million-unit claim, final 2 July; the court called the right to comfortably use restrooms "a fundamental and universal human right" and found the officer should have offered alternatives instead. Also reports a 2021 national human rights commission survey (591 trans respondents: 41% used another-gender restroom out of fear, 39% avoided food/drink, 36% skipped restroom use) and a 2021 regional district court ruling awarding 7 million units of local currency against a beauty academy that barred a trans student's restroom use.

National news agency wire (8 May 2024): a county within this state/province approved gender change for five transgender people without sex-reassignment surgery, ruling that requiring surgery would force people to violate their own physical integrity; prior court guidelines requiring surgery and proof of infertility are downgraded to reference-only status, though some courts still rely on them to dismiss applications; the case is expected to set precedent.

Progressive daily feature (21 Mar 2024): a youth LGBTQ+ support centre presented research on school facilities for trans students in the capital — survey of 86 trans/genderqueer students (Sept-Oct 2023) found 59 (69%) uncomfortable using school restrooms, drinking less water and leaving school early to avoid involuntary outing; another city's study of 208 students found 39% mistreated for gender identity/orientation; advocacy targets amendments to the educational-facilities act, school health act enforcement (single-occupant gender-neutral restrooms), school sports act (single-person showers/changing) and the violence-prevention act surveys.
blindLocalsOnly: School facilities are resident/student-facing: binary school restrooms leave 69% of trans students surveyed (86 respondents) uncomfortable, with documented patterns of avoiding water and leaving school early to avoid outing, and 39% mistreatment reported in another city's study (208 respondents); legislative advocacy for gender-neutral single-occupant restrooms and inclusive school rules concerns the domestic school system, which foreign visitors do not enter.
